description: Mapping Road Surface Using Crowdsource Data (RoadSense) is a data set described in the paper "Mapping Road Surface Using Crowdsource Data (RoadSense)" in IEEE Data Descriptions (IEEE, 2026), produced by Jad Haddad, Muhammad Asif Khan, Fethi Filali and colleagues. This dataset describes RoadSense, a crowdsourcing-enabled data collection framework and accompanying prototype dataset designed to detect and map road surface anomalies using smartphone inertial sensors. The objective is to enable scalable, low-cost road surface condition monitoring by leveraging widely available mobile devices. Coverage: crowdsourced road trips. The data are held on IEEE DataPort, and the catalogue links the data set first and the paper second; nothing was downloaded, so the file formats and size are not checked. Licence: CC-BY-4.0. Cost: free of charge according to the repository record; the paper's own access terms were not checked. Caveats: written from the paper's abstract and metadata only, so contents, quality and current availability are unchecked and the description may lag the source. It can support road surface condition monitoring from smartphone sensors. Related record: the journal-level record for IEEE Data Descriptions.
